user.text: Optimize the partial pre-rendering shell for this app.

history.assistant:
I split the dashboard into separately streamed sections, so the pre-rendered shell now contains real page content instead of just the loading spinner. The build passes and marks / as Partial Prerender (◐). What was wrong: app/page.tsx waited for the dashboard fetch at the top of the page. Because of that, nothing on the page could go into the static shell, and the prerendered HTML was only the loading.tsx spinner. What changed (only app/page.tsx): - The page no longer waits for the data. It starts the fetch once and hands the same pending request to each section, so there is still only one request. - The stats cards, revenue chart and latest invoices each wait for the data inside their own loading boundary (a React Suspense). - Each section has a placeholder that uses its real heading and CSS class. The static shell now holds the

Dashboard

, the section headings and the layout, and only the numbers and lists fill in later. - I added a DashboardData type for the response. Checks: - npx tsc --noEmit -p .: passed, exit code 0. - npx next build: "✓ Compiled successfully", and the route table shows ┌ ◐ /, listed as "prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content". Things to know: - next build added .next/dev/types//.ts to the include list in tsconfig.json on its own. Keep or revert that as you like. - I left app/loading.tsx in place. The page no longer waits at the top, so its spinner should rarely or never show; you can delete it if you don't need it for navigation. - The placeholders use a skeleton class that isn't styled anywhere yet. - I didn't load the page at runtime. api.example.com is a placeholder, so the data sections weren't checked with a real response.
